featured.title: US–Iran Fighting Escalates Again
featured.content: US forces struck two Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island, according to a US official cited by Reuters. Iran's Revolutionary Guards subsequently said they launched ballistic missiles at two US bases in Jordan in response. The escalation comes as the Strait of Hormuz remains central to the wider conflict and global energy security.

articles.title: BREAKING: US Forces Strike Iranian Launchers on Larak Island
articles.description: US forces struck two Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island on Sunday, according to a US official cited by Reuters. The official said the launchers were preparing to deploy sea mines into the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Iran Says It Launched Ballistic Missiles at US Bases in Jordan
articles.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Monday that they launched ballistic missiles at the King Hussein and Al Azraq US bases in Jordan in response to the US attack on Larak Island. The claim was reported by Iranian media and remains part of the rapidly developing conflict.
articles.imageQuery: Iran ballistic missile Jordan US military base

articles.title: Trump Claims Kharg Island Is Under Heavy Attack
articles.description: US President Donald Trump said Iran's Kharg Island oil hub was being heavily attacked. Reuters reported that there was no immediate independent confirmation of the claim, and an accompanying video was identified as AI-generated.

articles.title: Global Energy Security Remains Under Pressure
articles.description: The latest US–Iran escalation is keeping the Strait of Hormuz at the centre of global energy concerns. Further disruption to shipping could affect oil prices, inflation and transportation costs internationally.

articles.title: North Cyprus Ferry Disaster Leaves Dead and Missing
articles.description: At least eight people died and 18 remained missing after a ferry carrying about 267 passengers and crew capsized off North Cyprus. Rescue operations and investigations are continuing, while the cause of the accident remains unclear.

articles.title: US–Iran Conflict Enters Another Dangerous Phase
articles.description: The latest exchange of military strikes between Washington and Tehran represents a fresh escalation in the conflict, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining a major strategic concern.
articles.imageQuery: US Iran military conflict Middle East

articles.title: Washington Faces Growing Energy and Security Risks
articles.description: The continuing conflict with Iran is creating additional challenges for US policymakers as military operations, maritime security and global energy markets remain closely connected.

articles.title: Germany Investigates Suspected Leipzig/Halle Airport Attack
articles.description: German authorities are preparing a response to a suspected drone attack involving Leipzig/Halle airport. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said officials were finalising their response, while the circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation.
articles.imageQuery: Leipzig Halle airport Germany drone investigation

articles.title: EU Approves €6.1 Billion Defence Support for Ukraine
articles.description: The European Commission approved an additional €6.1 billion in financial support for Ukraine's defence on August 24. The package includes procurement of air-defence systems, missiles, ammunition and radar equipment.
articles.imageQuery: European Ukraine defence support air defence

articles.title: North Cyprus Ferry Disaster Triggers Rescue Operation
articles.description: Rescue teams are continuing operations after a passenger ferry capsized off Kyrenia. Survivors were rescued from the overturned vessel while authorities investigate what caused the disaster.

articles.title: Niger Army Regains Control of Key Airbase
articles.description: Niger's army says it regained control of a key military airbase after mutinous soldiers attacked it. The mutiny represents another challenge for Niger's military-led government.

articles.title: Niger Military Unrest Raises Questions About Army Cohesion
articles.description: The attack by mutinous soldiers highlights tensions within Niger's armed forces as the military-led government continues its fight against jihadist groups.

articles.title: Guinea-Bissau Holds Constitutional Referendum
articles.description: Voters in Guinea-Bissau are taking part in a referendum on proposed constitutional reforms that would significantly expand presidential powers. The vote comes amid continuing political instability following last year's military takeover.

articles.title: Nigeria's Kidnapping Crisis Remains a Major Security Concern
articles.description: Nigeria continues to face serious pressure from kidnapping networks. A security study cited by Reuters estimated that kidnappers collected almost $5.8 million in ransom payments from civilian abductions over the past year.

articles.title: Moody's Changes Nigeria's Outlook to Positive
articles.description: Moody's has changed Nigeria's sovereign outlook from stable to positive while maintaining its B3 rating. The agency cited stronger foreign-exchange reserves and better-than-expected economic growth.

articles.title: Energy Shock Continues to Influence Global Markets
articles.description: Investors are closely monitoring developments around the Middle East and Strait of Hormuz because further disruption could push energy prices higher and increase inflationary pressure.

articles.title: Oil Markets Remain Sensitive to US–Iran Escalation
articles.description: The latest military exchanges between the US and Iran are keeping oil and shipping markets on alert. Any prolonged disruption around Hormuz could have significant economic consequences.

articles.title: Nigeria's Improved Moody's Outlook Supports Investor Confidence
articles.description: Moody's positive outlook reflects stronger external resilience and economic growth, although Nigeria continues to face fiscal pressure and debt-affordability challenges.

articles.title: China–US Semiconductor Tensions Continue
articles.description: Chinese memory-chip manufacturer CXMT's legal dispute with the US Department of Defense remains part of the broader technology rivalry between Washington and Beijing.

articles.title: AI-Generated Video Highlights Need for Verification
articles.description: Reuters reported that a video accompanying claims about attacks on Iran's Kharg Island was AI-generated. The development highlights the growing challenge of distinguishing authentic footage from synthetic media during breaking news events.
articles.imageQuery: AI generated video artificial intelligence technology

articles.title: AI Continues to Transform Global Information Flows
articles.description: Artificial intelligence is increasingly affecting how breaking news is produced, shared and verified, making reliable sourcing and careful editorial checks more important during fast-moving crises.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: Security dominates today's international agenda. The US–Iran conflict has entered another dangerous phase following US strikes on Iranian launchers and Iran's reported missile response against US bases in Jordan. Niger's army says it has regained control of a key airbase after a mutiny. Guinea-Bissau is holding a closely watched constitutional referendum. Nigeria continues to confront serious insecurity while receiving a more positive economic outlook from Moody's. Europe is dealing with the aftermath of a deadly ferry disaster off North Cyprus and continuing investigations into the suspected Leipzig/Halle airport attack.

bigQuestion: As tensions rise across different parts of the world, can diplomacy still prevent today's conflicts from becoming tomorrow's larger crises?
quoteOfTheDay: When the world around you becomes uncertain, let your values remain certain. Keep learning, keep growing, and keep choosing hope.
